title: Developer scoping a transit-oriented infill on a COR corridor site

persona.description: Developer evaluating a 5–7 storey mixed-use building near a major bus terminal

turns.user_message: Hey, I'm scoping a mixed-use infill project at 6960 Mumford Road in Halifax — it's zoned COR under the Regional Centre Land Use By-Law. Before I go too deep into design, can you confirm what the maximum FAR and building height limits are for this site? I need to understand the envelope before I talk to my architect.

Got it on the envelope. Now, Mumford Road is a major transit corridor so I'm planning ground-floor retail or service commercial with residential above. What are the ground floor use requirements in the COR zone — is active commercial frontage mandatory, or just permitted? I want to know if I'm locked into it or if I have flexibility.

Good to know. What about the streetwall requirements along the Mumford Road frontage? I'm thinking of a podium-and-tower form — is there a minimum streetwall height or a build-to-line that would affect how close I need to push the building face to the street? And what are the front and side setback standards for COR specifically?

This is a transit-oriented site, so I'm trying to minimize surface parking. What are the minimum parking requirements for a mixed-use residential-over-commercial development in the COR zone? Is there any parking reduction available given the transit proximity, and does structured or underground parking count the same way toward satisfying the requirement?

One more critical piece — the parking layout and access will need site plan approval based on section 15(a) of the by-law. What else on this project would trigger site plan approval, and is there any discretionary approval or variance process I should be aware of if my proposed FAR or height pushes above the as-of-right limits? I need to map out the full approval timeline for my investors.
